native_result.query: In the PCA conducted on forms of capital, analyzed in hundred-year time slices, how are the symbolic capital components such as house size, daggers, and hatchets/swords characterized in terms of their values on the first principal component (PC1) and distribution across the second principal component (PC2)?
native_result.HypoA: Symbolic capital components such as house size, the number of daggers, and hatchets/swords are characterized by negative values on the first principal component (PC1) and exhibit a wide distribution of values on the second principal component (PC2). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In the PCA on the 12 forms-of-capital indicators across the 39 century bins (BCE 4300→500), the three symbolic-capital components — house size (Zhausgr), daggers (ZDolch) and hatchets/swords (ZAxtSchwert) — load on PC1 (30.3% variance, sign aligned so Pottery Form is positive) with the same sign and similar moderate magnitudes (−0.23, −0.27, −0.30; 5–9% PC1 contribution each), forming a tight co-varying cluster that distinguishes them jointly from the burial-display/pottery pole on the opposite end of the axis. On PC2 (19.5% variance; cumulative 49.8%) the three indicators are strongly asymmetric: house size carries a moderate positive loading (+0.33, ≈11% of PC2 variance) while daggers (+0.07) and hatchets/swords (+0.05) sit essentially at zero, so symbolic capital on PC2 is carried almost entirely by house size. Across the 100-yr slices PC2 scores are broadly dispersed — range [−3.70, +2.54] = 6.23 wide, median +0.34, IQR ≈ ±0.99, with 59% of bins (23 of 39) positive — exhibiting a slight positive central tendency and a strong negative outlier tail driven by the three identical deep-prehistoric bins (BCE 4300–4100). Synthesis: symbolic capital is unified and moderate on PC1, but split on PC2 — house size drives the secondary axis while daggers and hatchets/swords are quasi-orthogonal to it, so the "distribution along PC2" of symbolic capital effectively reduces to the house-size trajectory, which is itself widely spread but mildly positive across most century slices.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Load data/capital.csv (39×15), parse comma decimals → float in the 12 Z columns, drop group/color. 2) Verify pre-standardization: means ≈ 0 (max |μ|=0.00128) but stds unequal (min 0.53 for ZSichel, max 0.99); re-standardize each column to exact (mean 0, std 1) → 39×12 standardized matrix. 3) Run a single PCA via numpy.linalg.svd on the centered 39×12 matrix (sklearn unavailable; mathematically equivalent to sklearn.PCA(n_components=12)). 4) Sign-align per researcher: PC1 flipped so ZKeform loading is positive (raw = −0.3529 → flipped); PC2 sign aligned so largest-|loading| variable is positive (ZBeil at +0.4706 was already positive → no flip). 5) Extract full 12×12 PC1..PC12 loadings and per-PC1/PC2 contribution shares; produce focused row-table for Zhausgr/ZDolch/ZAxtSchwert. 6) Compute per-BCE-bin PC1..PC12 scores; characterize PC2 score distribution (min/max/range/median/Q1/Q3/IQR/frac_positive). 7) Save all artefacts (.py, .md, standardized matrix, loadings, scores, focused table, summary.json, run log) under artifacts/.
